title: Spot the bug
intro: Each short program runs without a compile error, yet prints the wrong thing or crashes. Read what it prints, click the line with the bug, then say why it is wrong.

notes.1: Line 2 is fine: `split(" ")` cuts the line at each space, and `parts[1]` is `"stop"`.

notes.0: Line 1 is fine: `toLowerCase()` returns `"oak"`, and `typed` catches it.

explain.text: `==` asks whether two arrows point at the same object, and a String built while the program runs is not the pooled literal
`==` ignores upper and lower case, so it matches the wrong text
a String must be compared with a literal in single quotes

rounds.right: Fixed: `{fix}` compares the text, so it matches however the String was made.

why.line: Line {n} does what it says. Which line makes it print something other than what it should?
why.case: `==` doesn't look at the text at all, so case doesn't come into it: it only checks whether the two arrows point at the same object.
why.quotes: Single quotes make a `char`, not a String. The literal is fine; the problem is how the two are compared.

explain.text: the call builds a new String and returns it, but nothing catches it: the variable still points at the old text
the call changes the String, but `println` shows a copy made before the change
the call has to come after the `println` to take effect

rounds.right: Fixed: `{fix}` catches the new String, so the variable now points at it.

why.line: Line {n} is fine as it is. Which line does work and then loses it?
why.copy: A String can never change, so there is no 'before' copy: the call made a new String, and the line dropped it.
why.order: Moving the line wouldn't help: the call returns its result, and this line doesn't keep it.

explain.text: `substring` leaves out its end index, so the end must be one past the last character wanted
indexes start at 1, so every index needs 1 added
the second argument of `substring` is how many characters to take

rounds.right: Fixed: `{fix}` ends one past the last character wanted, because the end index is left out.

why.line: Line {n} is fine. The output is one character short: which line cuts the text?
why.one: Indexes start at 0, and the begin index here is right. Look at where it stops.
why.length: The second argument is an index, the first one not included, not a count of characters.

notes.0: Line 1 is allowed: a String variable may hold `null`. The trouble starts when something calls a method on it.
Line 1 is allowed: a String variable may hold `null`. The trouble starts when something calls a method on it.
notes.1: Line 2 is fine: `+` turns `null` into the text `null`, so it prints `Name: null`. Which line crashed?

explain.text: the variable holds `null`, so there is no object to call the method on: a `NullPointerException`
`null` is the same as `""`, so the method answers the wrong way round

rounds.right: Fixed: `{fix}` checks for `null` first, so the method only ever runs on a real object.

why.line: Line {n} is fine. Read the console: which call was made on `null`?
why.empty: `null` is not an empty String: it is no object at all. `""` is an object with no characters.
why.plus: `+` can join `null`: it turns it into the text `null`. The crash comes from calling a method on it.
